title: Learned screening identifies liver-expression differences across archived cohorts
summary: Three feature-selection methods nominated five expression candidates for fatty liver disease. The source reports concordant expression differences in pooled external liver datasets, with individual-marker AUCs of 0.652–0.751. This is a retrospective tissue association, not a diagnostic test or a causal immune mechanism.
ai_technology: LASSO; support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination; random forest

source_review.scope: Primary front;computational Methods2.1,2.5 and Results3.4–3.5;primary deposited metadata status;experimental procedures not reviewed

evidence.ai_role: LASSO,SVM-RFE and random forest fitted disease-label feature selectors; their intersection selected BBOX1,FOSB,NR4A2,RAB26 and SOCS2 for later expression comparisons.
evidence.tested: Training combined50 disease and31 control samples. External pooled datasets contained271 disease and85 control samples; source-reported marker AUCs were0.734,0.751,0.709,0.670 and0.652.
evidence.unknown: Original datasets and batch correction can confound retrospective comparisons; no prospective or separate-team clinical validation is established. BBOX1 was not significantly different in the206-case/10-control dataset alone, despite significance in the pooled set. Source figure captions inconsistently call the five-marker intersection seven markers; RF selection counts also vary. Earlier roles of FOSB and SOCS2 are acknowledged. Protein experiments, mechanistic claims and inferred immune-cell causality are outside this represented result.
